reviews.text: Manchester By the Sea may be a somber and dour experience, but it’s one full of hope that people can survive grief.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Lonergan interrogates the realities of grief with sober restraint.
reviews.author: Demitra Kampakis

reviews.text: Manchester overflows with ripe dialogue, developed characters, and a toughmindedness that resists the all-American bromide that with a little emotional elbow grease, anyone can transcend their past and get on with it.
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: There are some awfully good moments in "Manchester by the Sea," and there aren’t really any awful moments.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Lonergan balances unrecoverable anguish with tender warmth in Manchester by the Sea, a film that considers a character unable to forgive himself and hesitant to engage with anyone ever again.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: A showcase in the power of understatement...Manchester By The Sea achieves great impact by feeling devastatingly real.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a study of guilt and the complexity of recovering from it. A modern day tragedy that will surely bring tears but also bring hope that Lee may one day say goodbye to his past and forgive himself.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea defies description in a really, really good way. It's not flashy or formulaic in the way some fish-out-of-water stories are. Instead, the story of a quietly suffering man
reviews.author: Hosea Rupprecht

reviews.text: The sort of understated, under-the-radar drama that can use all the help it can get to stand out in an increasingly overcrowded marketplace.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Arguably 2016's most notable film about loss and grief, one that tells its story with the scope of an epic while never leaving the Boston area.
reviews.author: Ian Brill

reviews.text: It deals with very real, very difficult human situations but does so with honesty and a great deal of unexpected humour and wisdom.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The great moments are haunting, though they're buried deep within a numbing amount of extraneous normalcy.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Manchester By The Sea doesn't play by the rules and that is its greatest asset as a film. It will break even the toughest cynic in the world.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Despite the heart-breaking premise, the film is filled with unexpected moments of humour and warmth.
reviews.author: Film Companion Staff

reviews.text: Becomes nothing short of a remarkable piece of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan's film is a humane examination of the suffering of an ordinary man, whose terrible personal tragedy has emotionally crippled him.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: Whilst Manchester by the Sea didn't resonate with me entirely, it's hard to deny that capture of realism which works so well.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Lonergan masterfully directs a humane film that explores a very simple concept, that is then expanded to reveal a redemption and mourning story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: The film is the portrait not of a man but of his self-loathing, which needs an environment and community to reflect off of, like the moon reflects sunlight.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: Lonergan, who also writes the solid script, adjusts the film's gloomy background with cautious authorship that, while seemingly simple, is shamelessly profound. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: The film's only downside is that it reminds us how damn long it takes Lonergan to write and direct a movie. But if the results are this extraordinary, we'll somehow find a way to fill the gaps.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is one of the best films of the year. It's cathartic, and it reminds us that even in the dark waters of grief, we're never truly alone.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: The writer/director doesn't avoid the leg work and turns those minor indignities of everyday life into representations of inner turmoil.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Despite the misery involved in this highly-emotional film, the finely-tuned script, along with outstanding performances, is reason enough to see this...
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea will restore your faith in the movies.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a deeply affecting drama with a captivating turn by Casey Affleck.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Though it sometimes settles into a monotonous dead zone, Manchester by the Sea is an exacting familial drama, rigidly held in place by a commendable supporting cast and what stands as Casey Affleck's most generous performance to date.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Even if Manchester were not so technically accomplished and beautifully acted, it would still stand as a unique work, simply because you get the ineffable sense that the director has experienced himself what he's depicting on screen
reviews.author: Rhys Tarling

reviews.text: It's stunning, and Casey Affleck will just break your heart into splinters.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: Its visual modesty conveys the feeling that the director protects his characters, respecting their pain by diverting their eyes and giving them some space. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: Lucas Hedges buoys up every scene he's in. And in a compact but explosive role, Michelle Williams brings the whole movie to a standstill with one devastating scene.
reviews.author: Brian D. Johnson

reviews.text: Manchester maintains a masterful balance of tragedy and humor.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Takes us to a place that few films have ever gone, with a depth and maturity that is a rare commodity in modern cinema.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is pretentious but fantastic performances and a realistic depiction of what grief really looks like elevates this above the normal Oscar bait.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a visceral cinematic experience and a beautiful accomplishment.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: MANCHESTER BY THE SEA may not have the neat resolution you want, but it features tangible characters whose lives you want to be a part of and an unforgettable experience that's rich with all of life's pain and joy.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: If you can handle it, the end experience is worth it.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is at once hilarious and tragic without ever feeling in conflict with itself.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is powerful stuff. No emotional punches are pulled; the blows landed on Lee land just as heavily on the audience.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The cinematography captures the setting exquisitely, the performances are top-notch, and the directing and writing, both courtesy of Kenneth Lonergan, is a marvel to behold.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Directed and written by Kenneth Lonergan, Manchester by the Sea pulls you in gently and it's soberly absorbing.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Devastadora y conmovedora en igual medida, Manchester frente al mar es un drama excelentemente dirigido que está al servicio del excepcional talento de Casey Affleck y el resto del reparto. Te romperá el corazón.
reviews.author: Julio Fernando Navas

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is paralytic in power.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: The masterful screenplay comes to life with such vibrancy that it's difficult to remember that viewers are watching a movie rather than peeking on a Boston family's real lives
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: Its sadness is its strength as it emphasizes the ordinariness of grief...
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a stunningly well acted, searingly honest, complex film. Compulsory viewing.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Casey Affleck delivers what most will call one of the best performances of his career and will most likely earn him an Oscar nod in January.
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams

reviews.text: An emotionally resonant tearjerker/masterful character study with Casey Affleck stepping up to the plate to claim some majorly overdue attention.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The film really is a work of deft narrative finesse. The use of flashbacks - often a syrupy or lazy trope - is expert from both a tonal and dramaturgical perspective.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: This is a stunning piece of storytelling that pulls viewers into its emotionally honest story and drives them through a wide range of emotions throughout the layers of its construction.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: It is a film with a commitment to verisimilitude that is both admirable and occasionally frustrating.
reviews.author: Sam Parker

reviews.text: I loved how [Lonergan] juxtaposes the people of the titular setting with the actual setting itself, which both hides life's tragedies and yet also offers an elegiac space for peace and safety.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: A near-perfect movie.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: What it ends up becoming is so much more...you won't be able to prepare for this movie, you'll just have to let it wash over you.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: Tragically depressing yet profound in its level of character.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: As a blue and grey movie with dangerous flashes of color, flashbacks are beautiful and understated in a completely interwoven story from playwright Lonergan.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: This is a moving and truthful examination of one family's sorrow and dysfunction and their resigned acceptance that some losses can never be replaced.
reviews.author: Glynis Costin

reviews.text: Lonergan's picture could have tipped easily into mawkishness, but all concerned exercise painstaking restraint.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: If you've never seen "You Can Count on Me," do yourself a favor and seek it out. And do not miss "Manchester by the Sea," because it will be the movie everyone will be talking about, and you will never forget the (tear-soaked) experience.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: Most of the film feels numb, because Affleck lives in an emotionally closed off bubble and seems like he's just going through the motions; Williams is the one to coax the many unresolved feelings to the forefront.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Lonergan's fidgety, often riotous film refuses to sit still... It demands movement and conversation, no matter how uncomfortable or ill advised the process may be.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: Even when faced with the prospect of personal growth, the New York-based filmmaker's fallible, fascinating characters keep reverting to old patterns. Try as they might, these leopards can't change their spots.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan's Manchester by the Sea is a poignant, evocative portrait of grief.
reviews.author: Abbey Bender

reviews.text: Despite the film's elaborate flashback structure, it does not get bogged down in plot. It reveals each character in his or her own time.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: What makes the film stand apart isn't its authentic flavours or visceral performances, but the story's integrity - a rare commitment to truth that deserves to be seen.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" is a contemporary exploration of mourning that will probably leave its mark on the cinematographic landscape. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Director/writer Kenneth Lonergan's expressive and impactful drama...is a complex and thoughtful depiction of the grieving process.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Even if abandonment is a theme of the movie, Manchester by the Sea does not for a minute abandon its human element.
reviews.author: Uri Klein

reviews.text: ... it is a minimalist story about any life that, at a certain moment, collapses and becomes a crater. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Campeny

reviews.text: Williams is stunning in a heartbreaking attempt at reconciliation, but too much of the film feels needlessly padded, as its 137-minute running time easily could have been shaved by at least a half hour.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: Despite a couple of minor false steps ... Manchester by the Sea is a wonderfully haunting portrayal of grief and regret - worth seeing if none-other than for Affleck's performance alone.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: ... a film about affective relationships, and family relationships... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: "I can't beat it" - Those four small but powerful words might be the most emotional piece of dialogue heard all year.
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: ...Casey Affleck delivers one of his strongest performances to date.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: An emotionally flush, simmering melodrama of sorrow surrounding a death in small Massachusetts family that echoes and underlines older trauma...
reviews.author: Daniel Kasman

reviews.text: The prickly warmth, specificity, and gallows humour that is Lonergan's stock in trade is gradually diluted by the generic mechanics of an important prestige picture.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonegran's films are governed by the laws of slow combustion. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: It's beautifully acted, particularly by Affleck, but so steeped in multi-layered misery that you do worry about its prospects at the box office. Nevertheless, I urge you to go and see it.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is Kenneth Lonergan's third film, and his strongest result yet.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Casey Affleck has earned much praise for his performance in this drama and deservedly so.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is perfectly observed in every detail, from its writing and performances (Affleck and Michelle Williams as his ex wife are locks for Oscar nominations) to its set decorations (someone understands the clutter of real life).
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: [Michelle] Williams has only a few scenes but makes her mark in all of them.
reviews.author: Anwen Crawford

reviews.text: Affleck lives in every frame, carrying Manchester By the Sea along with him, toward a transcendent state of being that reminds us of our own moments of love irretrievably lost.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: [Manchester By the Sea] is a life-sized story about recognizably human characters whose dilemmas stay with us.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea, while not a great film, is an honest lesson in grief.
reviews.author: Martha K. Baker

reviews.text: Affleck seems to be trying a bit too hard, straining towards a profundity that he can't quite grasp.
reviews.author: Marc Mohan

reviews.text: The film retains a precision and grace throughout and even the occasional clanging bit doesn't detract that much.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: This is not a story that ties things up neatly with a bow; it depends so much on the unsaid that Affleck's understated and incredibly moving performance carries the film.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: In Manchester by the Sea, Kenneth Lonergan again explores the depth of grief.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Despite its obvious Oscar-bait trappings, Kenneth Lonergan's Manchester by the Sea is plagued by outdated ideas about masculinity and weak supporting characters.
reviews.author: Alex Heeney

reviews.text: Despite all the crummy ones, there's always the chance you'll stumble across one like this - a movie so powerful, so beautifully done on just about every level, that it's instantly etched in your memory. And your heart.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is so engrossing that our attention never wanders from what we are being shown on screen.
reviews.author: Francine Prose

reviews.text: Writer/director Kenneth Lonergan's MANCHESTER BY THE SEA made me leave the theater feeling empty... it could easily be filed away as just another white male angst narrative.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: A gut-punching, heartbreaking movie, with Affleck's Lee in the epicentre ... a perfect role for the under-appreciated actor.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: The movie is pulsating with urgency and feeling, not deadened by the suggestive framework of its premise. I could not take my eyes off any of these people.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: Some emotional wounds can't be healed. Manchester by the Sea... takes on that proposition in family drama, or rather a drama about what we do for family even when there are things we can't do for ourselves.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: A superb family melodrama built in two times and centered on the complex figure of Lee Chandler. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan, the writer/director of You Can Count on Me, another finely nuanced film on difficult families and a personal favorite of mine, has done it again here.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: With an outstanding set and poignant performances, the winner of the Academy Awards for best original script and best actor is a must-see. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernando Moreno

reviews.text: Lonergan's film seems to suggest that life simply carries on, and it's up to us to find the courage to keep up with it. His thoughtful filmmaking style [...] is a delicate, welcome consolation.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: Lonergan and his cast perfect the art of the verbal squabble, funny and sad, vibrant and testy. It feels like life.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It's not an easy movie, and the slow pace might bore some viewers, but it's the perfect film for those who are looking for a mature and believable story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Manchester by the sea is a film full of a delicate beauty available to anyone who has the patience to keep up. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Paz

reviews.text: Devastatingly relatable and sincerely affecting.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A film that has a rhythmic sensitive pulse of a sweetly surprising dozen temporary swings and great award-winning performances. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Ayala Blanco

reviews.text: Despite the enormous emotional load that it drops on the viewer and the sadness that it brings, it's a grat film that makes us reflect on how fortunate we are to be able to spend time with our loved ones. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Iván Belmont

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a quiet, contemplative film that blends the most extreme depths of mourning with lashings of playful humour and explosions of anger.
reviews.author: Alex Casey

reviews.text: There are no contrivances, no manipulations, no false notes. Lonergan's film rings true as the complex relationships and multi-layered intricacies of grief find a compass that points to calmer waters. Prepare to be moved. This is one of the year's best.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: A film that can provoke the greatest laughter and then strike with an overwhelming dramatic force. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: A daring and original film that in the middle of its drama results in frankly funny moments. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: A great movie that addresses the issue of death, facing the feelings of mourning and how we process them, and where Cassey Aflleck gives us one of the most human performances. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario P. Székely

reviews.text: A film where the music is selected with exquisite taste and frames every sequence to reach the heart of the viewers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucero Solórzano

reviews.text: A devastating and poignant x-ray, presented in a poetic and painful way, on the limitations of the soul; The cast makes this throbbing drama work on other levels. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Ruiz

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a captivating family drama that pulls you into its little world through brilliant, Oscar-nominated writing and directing from Kenneth Lonergan and a top-notch ensemble that features a trio of Oscar-nominated performances.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Adopting a jigsaw-like structure, as past memories impinge on the present, Lonergan layers his characters with an enviable emotional complexity.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea defies Hollywood notion that all misfortune has an ulterior purpose or motive and that every dramatic arc must culminate in a positive change. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: A film that gives the sensation of being dragged by a slow tide taking us to our destination in the middle of a cloudy day, with nothing around able makes us smile. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: A film that swings subtly between tragedy and melodrama, avoids emotional blackmail and travels very effectively, through a series of retrospective scenes and flashbacks. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: A drama that is worth reviewing to analyze the ways in which we say to face the moments that define our lives with the remarkable performance of Casey Affleck, who carries the weight of history with strength. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Miguel Ravelo

reviews.text: A film with really outstanding performances with situations and emotions of a subtly depressive scent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: A film about loss and guilt, from a natural and even fun perspective. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Chris Lehmann

reviews.text: A somber, incredibly compelling masterpiece...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: With its extraordinary aesthetic of the uncomfortable, the film manages to find a balance between the misfortune and the sudden luminosity of the laughter. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alonso Díaz de la Vega

reviews.text: A vortex of tragedy, where not only one of the best works of its protagonist actor truly stands out, but also the simple but attractive photography by Jody Lee Lipes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gonzalo Lira Galván

reviews.text: Writer-director Lonergan's tight editing keeps the story moving forward while his ear for naturalistic dialogue lends authenticity.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Thrives on its main character being articulate by being inarticulate.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A very powerful and outstanding drama in which there's also some space for humor and its actors do an impressive job, especially a Casey Affleck. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Every single actor involved in this picture, from the leads to the extras, is magnificent.
reviews.author: Anthony Ray Bench

reviews.text: This is an exquisitely well-told tale about the way we deal with trauma and loss.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: A self-indulgent and irritating film of someone bent on telling a tragedy in a different way, stripping it of melodramatic resources. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: Miraculously, this lengthy, achingly sad story is very entertaining and leaves you wanting more. An undercurrent of dry humour makes its way into even the most tragic of sequences.
reviews.author: Nick Dent

reviews.text: [A] masterful, often devastating film.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Let's call this a strange artifact, much deeper, lucid and relevant than a simple drama. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: What you may not have heard is that, for the vast majority of its running time, it is very, very funny ... A great film. It is thoroughly involving, deeply moving, and sparkles with humanity.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea isn't concerned with finality or even redemption, rather the mess of life, unmoored from the belief that everything will be okay.
reviews.author: Conor Bateman

reviews.text: A solid drama with tints of posthumor that consolidates Casey Affleck as a great actor and not just as 'Ben's brother'. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Marañón

reviews.text: While terribly, even hauntingly painful at times, Manchester by the Sea is also generously funny, which is rather odd given that it's a film about grief, self-loathing, forgiveness and not-so-happy families.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: This superbly written and acted American drama extracts so many perfect moments from one man's imperfect mourning process that it simply must be hailed as one of the best films you will see in 2017.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: In Manchester by the Sea, writer-director Kenneth Lonergan studies this brand of maleness -- defined by emotional reluctance and reticence -- while adroitly examining how damaging these paralysing strictures can be.
reviews.author: Dave Crewe

reviews.text: A powerful and sometimes unexpectedly humorous drama about a man who refuses to acknowledge his past even as the present insists on it.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea may be a potent examination of grief, family and self-imposed solitude, but it's also oddly life-affirming and uplifting.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Casey Affleck's performance in "Manchester By The Sea" is one of the most effectively crafted portrayals of the crippling weight of grief in recent movies.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Emotionally gruelling-yet somehow still funny-Manchester by the Sea magnificently covers the wide expanse of human experience.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: There is mordant humour here, rippled with moments of extraordinary tenderness, but at heart this is a grave, unconsoling and profoundly sad film.
reviews.author: Edward Lawrenson

reviews.text: Not a moment in the film is wasted; though on the long side, this is from start to finish a rewarding and strangely beautiful drama with a conclusion that is immensely satisfying in its touching understatement.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: There is an in-built drabness to the drama of Manchester by the Sea that, while never exactly boring, takes far too long to get to its sobering yet unremarkable payoff. We all enjoy a good downer, but not one that also manages to tire us out.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan is a master of writing real people, resplendent in their absurdity, staggering in their endurance of grief.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: What emerges is as subtle as it is shattering: ordinary, unshowy and, underneath, red raw with real feelings.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: With an outstandingly icy Casey Affleck as a mournful loner drawn back into his old fold, Kenneth Lonergan's New England community study is a masterful, darkly American account of a heart in the dead of January.
reviews.author: Nick Pinkerton

reviews.text: A quiet, thoughtful film meditating on the question of loss and those death leaves behind, director Kenneth Lonergan delivers a deeply humane portrayal of grief and those who choose to let it define them.
reviews.author: Ellen Murray

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is wistful, elegiac, and the sights and sounds of an Atlantic fishing town are beautifully captured by the muted cinematography of Jody Lee Lipes. But there are moments of high drama, even comedy.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: It's atmospheric and directed with precision and a strong feel for local character. But it's dreary when it should be devastating.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: Featuring award-worthy performances from its three leads, "Manchester by the Sea," is the perfect drama to off-set a multiplex full of Bad Santas and Dwayne Johnson.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: For all Lonergan's storytelling skills, Manchester by the Sea stands or falls on its central performance. Casey Affleck, outstandingly skilful at keeping his cards close to his chest, packs immense power into a study of incurable grief and guilt.
reviews.author: Jasper Rees

reviews.text: As painfully sad as all this sounds not once does the film feel forced or overdone. Yes there's tragedy, but it always sits believably alongside the everyday.
reviews.author: Andy Psyllides

reviews.text: Affleck is on electrifying form as Lee, a surly janitor living alone in a Boston suburb.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: An immensely sad story but one that finds glimmers of hope in the darkest corners of human experience.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Stunningly acted and superbly written, this is a heart-breaking study of loss and human connection that's shot through with raw emotion.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: Lonergan's film has the same qualities as an early Springsteen song -- a narrative filled with a haunting, pervasive sadness, filled with guilt and loss.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: Manchester By The Sea is the film that packs enough wallop to force movie fans, and cinema-goers in general, to sit up and take serious notice.
reviews.author: Amy West

reviews.text: Writer-director Kenneth Lonergan creates characters so vivid that they get deep under the skin, and he allows his actors to so fully inhabit them that they become unforgettable.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: In Manchester by the Sea, men are soulful and women are shallow, a gender gap that wounds this otherwise compelling drama.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: A drama of rage and grief that stands on the brink of the inexpressible.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: This is about life as it is lived in the real world, with unassuageable pain, loose ends untied, life lessons unlearned. Life with no narrative closure.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Each scene brims with self-contained humour and drama, regardless of whether it moves the story along or simply fills in background colour.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: That Manchester By The Sea is so absorbing is down to Lonergan's painstaking directorial style and to a superb Method-style performance from the lead actor.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea manages to do the seemingly impossible. It is a deeply moving study of coping with abject grief, yet it is not profoundly grim.
reviews.author: Sarah McIntyre

reviews.text: The bitterly cold New England landscape only serves to highlight the wintry hearts of its characters.
reviews.author: Allie Gemmill

reviews.text: Lonergan's static pace and over-obvious compositions attempt fake "realism," but each scene looks like an acting-class exercise.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Masterfully told and beautifully acted, Manchester By The Sea is a shattering yet graceful elegy of loss and grief.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: If ever there was a film that epitomised the saying 'no pain, no gain', this is it. Packs a real wallop.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: For all its moments of discord, Manchester By the Sea sings its lonely song with tremendous heart and soul.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea, for this reviewer at least, is a classic case of a film that is immensely admirable and yet all but impossible to even remotely like.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: ...moving, romantic, devastating, and hilarious.
reviews.author: Sophia Watson

reviews.text: Lonergan is so precise with his actors, the sense of place, and the level control of tone that you feel him methodically striving here to avoid false notes.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Writer-director Kenneth Lonergan has crafted a great screenplay for this film, filled with witty, observant dialog. I've not seen a film in recent memory which more accurately and convincingly reveals human nature.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea features brilliant work from director Kenneth Lonergan and all of its actors, especially Casey Affleck.
reviews.author: Jay Ledbetter

reviews.text: A shattering and surprisingly hilarious study of death, guilt and family centred on a revelatory performance by the good Affleck brother.
reviews.author: Jamie Dunn

reviews.text: A solid drama about grieving men and private hells.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Lonergan's dialogue, as always, is a thing of beauty.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: People are praising Casey Affleck's acting in Manchester By the Sea, and he'll probably get the Oscar for it-it's a solid, often surprising, sometimes monotonously drilling performance.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: There's warmth and a relief of humor to balance the weight, making Manchester not just an emotional punch, but a deeply entertaining one. It's one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan has crafted a film that speaks to the human condition without getting pretentious. Insight is rarely this accessible.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: I believe that the film is great. I also believe that I may never watch it again.
reviews.author: Rich Heldenfels

reviews.text: Led by Affleck's superior performance, the movie is an obvious awards season frontrunner, a bandwagon nearly filled. Get on board.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Approach Manchester by the Sea with caution.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: A completely breathtaking film about humans in crisis, presented with a muted but still sharp-witted aesthetic.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: its virtues far outweigh its problems, but Manchester by the Sea still feels like a film that isn't quite there
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: An emotionally-engaging tale of redemption certain to garner its share of accolades over the course of the awards season.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: Delicately acted [and] superbly realized.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: This sensitive and surprisingly funny drama is full of well-drawn characters.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: One of the finest films of the year -- or any year, for that matter.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Affleck, Williams devastating in "Manchester by the Sea."
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is an affecting examination of the grieving process, brought to life through strong direction and compelling performances.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: While [Longergan] retains his playwright's focus on the writing and acting elements of film, he's skilled enough as a cinematic storyteller that this leisurely paced 137-minute movie does not drag or suffer from any dead spots.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan has written quite a script.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: It's an extremely human story of how grief and depression can eat away at the soul and leave its victims a hollowed-out shell.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: This is a film lover's dream if you enjoy watching actors and filmmakers performing at the top of their game. (Full Content Review for Parents - Sexual Content, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Deep, rich characters and a story to match. This one is golden from top to bottom and deserves the accolades it's getting. One of my favorites this year.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Lonergan has a particular talent for laying people bare and showing how they work. You see yourself in his characters, and you want to help put them back together again.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: Despite the film's somber tone, there's a truth and honesty in Lonergan's surprisingly complex story that will weave its way into your heart.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: This is without question my favorite film of the year
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Another example of Lonergan's gift with storytelling and timing, taking a slow but engrossing journey into the ways of grief and responsibility, and doing so with an expert handling of humor, heart, and paralyzing pain.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The thing about a Kenneth Lonergan movie is that it feels like you're watching people, not actors. You're watching a world unfold, and not some form of fiction.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: The most textured, emotionally complex screenplay of the year, by some distance. Lonergan's filmmaking redefines epic. He has found something big and universal in the small, specific characters he shows us at hauntingly close proximity.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: The reliably affecting Affleck plays Lee like a prowling animal trapped in a small room.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: An elegant and spiritually sobering film about the ways in which guilt, loss, isolation and self-destruction can erode the foundations of our lives.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: (You'll be) totally absorbed by its remarkable humor, profound tragedy, and very human telling.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" sees its bleak premise to the end without giving in to most movies' terrible need to resolve the unresolvable.
reviews.author: Gary Shannon

reviews.text: One of those weird cases of a film that technically hits most of the appropriate marks, but is so lifeless it's hard to fully appreciate.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: A movie about regret and we all have regrets... it's just a matter of if we let those regrets define us. But, sometimes, we don't have that choice.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: The story is about how we get past trauma and how sometimes we don't but keep going all the same. And even that latter situation is not without a gleam of hope, as Manchester by the Sea slowly uncovers its broken but humane heart.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: It is, to be sure, one of the most affecting films of this surprising year. It's about how very much emotion some lives are required to contain silently while, for all the world, they function day to day.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a long, contemplative slice of New England life. It's also a near-lock for a best picture nomination, even though it could stand to lose a good 10 to 15 minutes.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: There's no facile, feel-good redemption here. But there may be hope.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: Unforced acting couples with a nuanced, insightful script to tell a story that, although seemingly simple, is achingly complex.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea paints a rich and touching portrait of a family's grief, and one man drawn back to deal with the past he tried to put behind him. It's a movie that will resonate in the heart long after the credits roll.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Yeah, it's heavy. It's also unexpectedly funny, deeply moving and almost unbearably wise when it comes to the labyrinthine workings of the human heart.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: What definites Manchester by the Sea is its humanity. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: The film is deeply sad at times, but leavened with dry humor and the fragile hope that some people can suffer tragedy and survive. Life goes on, even when you think it shouldn't.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: It is one of the most real, heartbreaking films you'll see. Lonergan's elegiac story is brutally honest -- and brutally real.
reviews.author: Laura DeMarco

reviews.text: Affleck's performance, equally haunting and electric, helps transform Lonergan's film from merely a dramatic showcase into an emotional powerhouse.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: The sadness of "Manchester by the Sea" is the kind of sadness that makes you feel more alive, rather than less, to the preciousness of things.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Very simply, Manchester by the Sea is one of the best films of 2016. Multiple Oscar nominations are in its future. Brace yourself and don't miss it.
reviews.author: Dan Hudak

reviews.text: Affleck is magnificent, but the movie is something less than that, because it can't completely overcome some built-in challenges. Even so, Manchester by the Sea deserves honors for being so different, and for working on the mind in a particular way
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Affleck puts his heart and soul in this role.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: A sensitive and occasionally stinging look at how death disrupts life.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The centerpiece of Kenneth Lonergan's drama Manchester by the Sea is a relatively short scene, a conversation between two characters that contains the most moving moments I've seen on screen in years.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: It's not a flashy film, nor is it perfect, but there is an honesty and deep-felt compassion that cannot be ignored.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a stunner, delivering in ways that defy easy description.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" is an award-caliber movie on all fronts and one that will stick with you long after it is over.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Lonergan's script and direction are pleasingly subtle, studded with nice little moments that help us understand the characters and help them understand each other.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: ... never really earns the responses it wants to elicit from its viewers.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: Its initial enigma seems to need no explanation; yet, once deciphered, the film does not falter but moves only deeper into the emotional territory it charts.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: It's painful and tragic, yet it's cut with elements of humor and laughter. Just like life.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan's Manchester By the Sea is the best film I've seen in 2016. But I'm honestly not sure I can watch it again.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea may take its time making itself heard, but you can count on it.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Gorgeously sad and occasionally very funny.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: Affleck gives the sort of crumpled, seething, fully lived-in performance that De Niro and Pacino gave in their primes, and he gets strong support from Michelle Williams, Kyle Chandler and Gretchen Mol.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: (Casey) Affleck gives the finest performance of his career. It is a measured portrait of a man so overwhelmed by shame and hurt that he seems to simply go through the motions of living.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: ...a portrait of a man who deals with grief by submerging it into the marrow of his bones.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: It's Affleck's movie to quietly own as layer upon layer of Irish impassivity is stripped away from his visage until the unspeakable can be spoken.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Lonergan found the right man in Affleck, standing stony-faced while others weep, his performance a master class in submerged feeling... But it's Williams who stuns, in the course of a single, astonishing dialogue toward the end of the film.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Not everything broken, this wise movie reminds us, can be mended.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" is one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: There's a funny sequence when Lonergan surprise-reveals that Lee fathered one, then two, then three children, who tumble out from the corners of the screen like squashed clowns.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Casey Affleck's visceral performance as the story's lead character, Lee Chandler, is essential to the film's excellence. All the film's key actors deliver matchless performances, but Affleck here has the role of his lifetime.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" is the latest installment in a body of work from an artist fascinated by how life marches on, with or without us, and how we scramble to keep up. Not everyone can, though.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: A heart-wrenching drama anchored by Affleck, who notches up yet another subtle, stunning performance.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: As pleasurable a viewing experience as a film about death could hope to be.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: A remarkable drama that seems made to win an Oscar and where the interpretation of Casey Affleck really stands out. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucía Ros Serra

reviews.text: Lonergan doesn't write dialogue that spells out details of the harrowing event. He leaves it to outstanding actors to convey the effect of the experience via facial expression and body language.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: Lonergan capitalizes on Affleck's vulnerability in a textured, cliche-free portrait of human survival without a conventional ending.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: In its broad strokes, Manchester by the Sea doesn't explore anything new...[but Lonergan] is the master of telling behavior and conversational nuance.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: A drama of rare power-a tale of human suffering that succeeds because of its love for its characters, rather than for their misfortunes.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: It's a beautifully made, skillfully acted effort, with an astonishing lead performance by Casey Affleck. (Splice Today)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Complex, layered, and respectful of the audience's intelligence and attention span.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Affleck is riveting as a broken man, a resonant metaphor for our times.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It's less a movie of aesthetics than of synesthesia, transmitting an unbearable burden of inner coldness and emptiness by means of warmhearted wonder.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: One of the year's best pictures.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Affleck's Lee is a figure too tragic even for Shakespeare. But his pain, and yes, his courage, is seared into our memories, making "Manchester" not just a place by the sea, but also a piece of our hearts.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: In the hands of Lonergan and his exceptional cast, the deceptively simple story becomes a shattering tale of shared grief that carries a powerful weight of emotional truth.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: [Writer/director Kenneth] Lonergan's film is a marvel of compassion and character-specific observation.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: ...a fairly fascinating character study...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: An unflinching, emotionally devastating tear-jerker.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: New Englanders, with both the dialog and locations, will feel at home in this small town saga, captured skillfully by cinematographer Jody Lee Lipes.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Too often here you feel the fingers of the writer, typing the story into existence, crafting it to its desired ends.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" is a masterpiece in a minor key, an exploration of grief that never lets its characters - or its audience - off the hook.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: An achingly graceful, heartfelt, working-class story about loss, grief, and family obligations.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: I've found it really hard to write about Manchester by the Sea, because it sunk into my bones so deeply it's hard to extract. Yet just thinking about it now, my heart is in my throat.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: A movie this deep and emotionally resonant, a movie about grown-ups without any kind of sales pitch in mind, is a beautiful and rare thing.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: It's a masterful, all-American tale that delves deep into the black hole of grief. At times, it can all be emotionally overwhelming - but isn't that a characteristic of a great movie?
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: "Manchester By the Sea" is a film of surpassing beauty and heart. Even at its most melancholy depths, it brims with candid, earnest, indefatigable life.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a film that knocks politely on the door of the mind, and the heart. The advice here is to let it in immediately.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea will almost certainly go down as the most devastating, heart-wrenching drama of 2016.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: If you open yourself to the experience, Lonergan's movies allow you to live with characters until they feel like people you know. Sometimes they're people you don't like very much. But somehow, by the end, they're your people.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea would probably be hailed as one of the year's best comedies if everybody in the audience didn't spend half of it sobbing.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Watching actor Casey Affleck, who looks like an eternally youthful choir boy, fight his inner demons is worth the price of admission alone.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: If you feel ashamed to be laughing, then Lonergan has got you exactly where he wants you-stirred and confounded, casting around for breaks in the cloud of sadness.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: There's a modesty here that's too often absent in fall prestige pictures, a sense that the director is protecting his characters, rather than exploiting them.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Despite confusing flashbacks with no discernible transitions, the acting is good enough to offset watching Affleck be depressed for 237 minutes.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: The meat of the plot is simple, but Lonergan adds layer on top of layer, adding great emotional complexity to this Shakespearean tragedy about grief and reconciliation with the past.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: It's hard to overstate the magnificence of Kenneth Lonergan's Manchester by the Sea.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Lonergan's wrought script pursues a simple man's life to its darkest place ... and sits there with him, until we understand.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: ... covers familiar thematic territory but conveys a genuine bittersweet poignancy that sidesteps clichés of family dysfunction and healing.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Writing this is making me sad all over again, so let's end by saying that the acting throughout is exceptional, and that Affleck is phenomenal: It's a black hole of a performance, and its pull is overpowering.
reviews.author: Tom Gliatto

reviews.text: [Lonergan's] latest, a quietly powerful examination of grief healed by a brothers' bond, is not only an emotional character-driven drama, but the best realization of Massachusetts on screen since "The Friends of Eddie Coyle."
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: With Manchester by the Sea, writer-director Kenneth Lonergan has delivered a quietly devastating sucker punch of a film about the persistence of hope in the face of unfathomable loss.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: Searing, insightful drama has intense themes, swearing.
reviews.author: S. Jhoanna Robledo

reviews.text: It's a magisterial achievement, a piece that captures the deepest recesses of the soul as they're found within the sort of ordinary man that's typically invisible on the big screen.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Because Lonergan is so true to the intricacies and rhythms of family strife, we trust his vision. When it comes time for the fade-out, he doesn't gussy up sorrow with a sunrise glow. Healing is hard.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: The funniest movie about grief ever made -- but that's far from the only remarkable thing about it.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: Fiercely human, bravely unsentimental and at times unnervingly hilarious, Manchester by the Sea washes over you, tossing and tumbling its disparate elements like a wild, bracing surf.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: Leaves you with the feeling you've just lived a whole separate lifetime and are re-entering, dazed, into your own.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: . . . a rare melodrama set in the world of men.
reviews.author: Violet LeVoit

reviews.text: Lonergan's latest, finely-tuned work shows an unbowed director plunging into the depths of grief.
reviews.author: Nicolas Rapold

reviews.text: You're left shaken with sorrow for the characters, and slowly filled with respect for them all.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Featuring a once-in-a-lifetime performance from Casey Affleck, Manchester will stay with you for weeks and months on an end after you see it.
reviews.author: Alex Welch

reviews.text: Featuring Casey Affleck in an Oscar-caliber performance, it's a deeply affecting little gem of a film, which should gently sweep filmgoers up in its melancholy tides.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is formula-free and one of a kind, with only as much resolution as the steely grip of the past will allow.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: No film this year has moved me more with its humor, heart and humanity. Engrave the name Casey Affleck on the Oscar for Best Actor right now, so extraordinary and engulfing is his performance.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Lonergan's film reveals itself as a wellspring of urgently needed compassion and grace.
reviews.author: Andrew Lapin

reviews.text: An emotional powerhouse with the weave of great literature.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" is a finely shaded portrait, a study in individual misery set in a place that is observed with care and affection.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: An exemplary film of such exceptional wisdom, beauty, clarity, sensitivity and emotional depth that I had to rub my eyes to believe it.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Lonergan has given us a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: "Manchester By the Sea" is heartbreaking yet somehow heartening, a film that just wallops you with its honesty, its authenticity and its access to despair.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: This is a staggering American drama, almost operatic in the heartbreak it chronicles, that's also attuned to everyday headaches, like forgetting where the car is parked and hitting your noggin on the freezer door.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: The result is a movie that, if never exactly a cathartic experience, carries you along in its clenched grip with an undeniable power. It's sad and funny and real.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: A poignant, surprisingly hilarious depiction of death, grieving, and small-town life.
reviews.author: April Wolfe

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea is a deeply affecting and wickedly funny masterpiece showcasing the maturation of men, from the broken man and his nephew at its heart to the drama's phenomenal filmmaker.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Affleck proves he can convey suffering as well as any actor alive. His trebly voice is cracked with pain. He comes with his own chill fog.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: This movie is a miracle: a stunningly intimate masterwork that wrenches, but still leaves the heart brimming.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Both one of saddest, most unflinchingly honest films ever made about death as well as a serious contender for the year's laugh riot. But one side doesn't cancel the other out.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: One of the most penetrating dramas of the year.
reviews.author: Daniel Eagan

reviews.text: Casey Affleck finds his best role as a depressed handyman whose life acquires meaning when he take charge of a teen nephew.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: This is a movie to see as soon as it comes out, before you've heard anything about the story.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: A drama that is always on the edge of emotional excess, but without crossing the limit. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Josefina Sartora

reviews.text: It oozes foreboding, yet Lonergan also conjures episodes of reviving wit.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: Casey Affleck... provides this overwhelmingly moving slow-burn drama about grief with its unforgettable lead performance.
reviews.author: Josef Braun

reviews.text: It's a story about grief and redemption, but it's told with the same complexity, depth and humour as [Lonergan's] debut film, You Can Count On Me.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Perhaps the most emotionally intelligent film you will see this year.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: The unparalleled honesty with which Lonergan tells his story lands it in a class all its own.
reviews.author: Michael Arbeiter

reviews.text: It is a film that emphatically deserves to be in the mix come awards-time, from a director who knows that you don't need fast-paced action or expensive tricks to conjure truly spectacular cinema.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: It cannot be stressed enough how much Casey Affleck's performance is the soul of Manchester by the Sea. It's a riveting turn that makes this bittersweet drama about New England pride and sorrow a true gem.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Williams maximizes each instance of her screen time. In as little as six minutes, she sets the screen on fire, almost unrecognizable in the player she portrays.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: The film gradually comes to its sense of exquisitely calibrated, hardened intimacy.
reviews.author: Christopher Gray

reviews.text: I've wondered often since seeing Manchester by the Sea how Lee is doing. Well, I hope.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Lonergan takes a broken man forced to return to the place that broke him and spins it into something magnificent.
reviews.author: Stephen Mayne

reviews.text: An interesting and well constructed film of which we will probably hear more about it the next months. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arturo Aguilar

reviews.text: Every aspect of the film seeks to make an emotional connection with the audience via specificity, and thanks to masterful work from Lonergan as writer and director and phenomenal performances from the entire ensemble cast, it is an absolute triumph.
reviews.author: Adam Chitwood

reviews.text: Definitely a personal film that reveals a brilliant director. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oscar Uriel

reviews.text: A truly incredible piece of cinema from a filmmaker that has marked himself as one of the most important working today.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: A devastating scene between Lee and his ex (Michelle Williams) is one of the best written -- and performed -- sequences I've ever seen on film.
reviews.author: Susan G. Cole

reviews.text: This is a pretty straightforward drama and not much more. There's nothing wrong with that. Just don't expect much of a deep seabed in this one.
reviews.author: Tina Hassannia

reviews.text: Sure to be one of the best films of this year, Manchester by the Sea delivers the soaring emotions of melodrama with a masterfully delicate touch.
reviews.author: Darren Ruecker

reviews.text: Manchester stands out for doing an old routine just right. It's not the next best thing, but it does justice to a familiar playbook.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: [A] beautifully textured, richly enveloping drama about how a death in the family forces a small-town New Englander to confront a past tragedy anew.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: A wrenching family tragedy is dramatized with the depth of a high-quality American stage piece in Manchester by the Sea.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: [Lonergan] immaculately constructs a layered, non-linear exploration of the ripple effects of loss and grief.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: It's wonderful to see Lonergan back at work, illuminating small and unremarkable lives with grace, wisdom, and humanity. He's made what might prove to be the most artful tearjerker of the year.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Lonergan weaves his way through many shades of grief, wise enough to understand that it never takes only one form.
reviews.author: Scott Renshaw

reviews.text: With its cathartic score and Lonergan's habit of underplaying his most dramatic moments, what could be an excruciating journey has a disarming grace
reviews.author: Chris Plante

reviews.text: The finest possible incarnation of the sort of starry, delicate drama that is a festival standard.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: A commanding, absorbing work in which the sum of its impact may be greater than any individual scenes.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Kenneth Lonergan's Manchester By The Sea will continue to haunt and endear for decades to come.
reviews.author: Josh Cabrita

reviews.text: Oscar-level acting by Casey Affleck in a career-defining part.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: This is pitch-perfect filmmaking, the kind that turns a hungry visionary into a popular last name. Rest assured, it's all earned. Manchester By the Sea is a hearty, rewarding drama audiences will remember for years.
reviews.author: Michael Roffman

reviews.text: [Sundance 2016] "Manchester by the Sea" finds the truth in each new moment even as the viewer longs for signs of hope that may never come.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: Manchester by the Sea plants a lot of seeds, but it doesn't grow.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: It captivates without ever calling attention to itself. It feels real. It feels honest.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Manchester-by-the-Sea is a study of family dysfunction and the worse loss imaginable, but one held back by the fact it's all filtered through Affleck's withdrawn lead.
reviews.author: Lanre Bakare

reviews.text: "Manchester by the Sea" is precise in its vision, universal in its application. It's one of this year's few great films.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Its world is cruel and chaotic, but it unfolds with purpose and grace.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: By the time the film ends, we know so much about these people and their town that they don't even need to articulate their feelings for us to understand them.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Manchester By The Sea is a meticulous, rich film: there's such a depth to this story of a man living with unbearable grief, a sense of time and place and the changing of the seasons, you feel you could almost touch it.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

synopsis: After the death of his older brother Joe, Lee Chandler (Casey Affleck) is shocked that Joe has made him sole guardian of his teenage nephew Patrick. Taking leave of his job as a janitor in Boston, Lee reluctantly returns to Manchester-by-the-Sea, the fishing village where his working-class family has lived for generations. There, he is forced to deal with a past that separated him from his wife, Randi (Michelle Williams), and the community where he was born and raised.
